authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with potential for new physics and applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic phases.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theory.
method: The authors present a pedagogical review of field-theoretic methods for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, covering path integrals, Doi-Peliti formalism, and renormalization group techniques.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic methods can be applied to a wide range of stochastic systems, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across multiple disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide crucial information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies on spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances and open questions in spin-glass dynamics.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to benefit from interdisciplinary approaches, with future opportunities in both fundamental and applied contexts.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a platform for studying topological order and fractionalized excitations.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental characterization of candidate materials (e.g., iridates, ruthenates).
result: Summarizes key properties such as chiral edge modes and the status of material candidates.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area with promising materials, but definitive experimental signatures are still sought.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, covering all facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an outlook on how these models can be incorporated into studies relevant to applications.
conclusion: The paper summarizes current theoretical approaches and suggests future directions for integrating them into applied research.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored. This review aims to bridge the gap between classical skyrmion physics and quantum phenomena.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, discussing quantum interactions underlying skyrmion formation and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: It highlights that skyrmions can exhibit quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement, and that their topological protection may be leveraged for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions offer a platform for exploring topological quantum phenomena and may have applications in quantum computing and spintronics, but further research is needed to realize practical quantum devices.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to test fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson-mediated interactions and highlights the most promising experimental approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a rich avenue for probing new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further experimental and theoretical work is needed.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where violations occur and identifies which assumptions are violated in each case.
result: It demonstrates that apparent violations arise from measurement conditions that do not satisfy the assumptions of the bounds, and that interesting material properties can be engineered.
conclusion: Classical thermodynamic bounds are not violated; rather, their assumptions must be carefully considered, and materials can be designed to circumvent these assumptions.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: The paper surveys various platforms (atomic, photonic, electronic) and techniques for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with quantum systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential to bridge condensed matter, high-energy physics, and quantum simulation.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, exploring whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement between massive particles.
result: Ongoing experiments aim to determine whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement, guiding theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Results from these experiments will inform the theoretical description of gravity on a laboratory scale.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory and can be reproduced classically, suggesting broader implications for foundations of physics and philosophy.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show that similar paradoxes arise in classical contexts, with implications for cosmology and epistemology.
method: The authors analyze Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, construct classical thought experiments with agent duplication, and identify a structural feature called 'Restriction A' that limits probabilistic descriptions of observations.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the core difficulty extends to other puzzles like the Boltzmann brain problem.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context beyond quantum foundations, addressing challenges in obtaining reliable predictions when observations are privately but not intersubjectively verifiable.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: This paper presents PyOpticL, an open-source Python library for modular optical system design, and demonstrates its use for trapped-ion qubit operations.
motivation: Complex optical design in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and scalability.
method: The authors developed PyOpticL, a code-to-CAD optical layout tool that uses beam-path simulation and dynamic routing to enable adaptive, path-based layouts. They created modular optical baseplates for common subsystems and demonstrated a full laser system for strontium trapped ions.
result: The system achieved over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates and was used for laser cooling and qubit state detection, showing the feasibility of modular optical systems for quantum computing.
conclusion: PyOpticL enables a new paradigm of design abstraction for optical systems, fostering open-source collaborative hardware design for AMO physics and quantum computing.

title: Sorting Prolate And Oblate Spheroids With A Diatomic Gas In A Magnetic Field
authors: Ruben Lier
abstract: For a gas of diatomic particles with a nonzero magnetic moment, the Senftleben–Beenakker effect implies that transport can be affected by a magnetic field even when the particles are charge neutral. In such a gas, two independent anisotropic odd viscosities are allowed by symmetry and can have opposite signs. We study the resulting odd-viscous Stokes flow around spheroids in the regime where the odd viscosities are small compared to the shear viscosity. Using a perturbative expansion around the spherical solution and the Lorentz reciprocal theorem, we compute the lift forces on oblate and prolate spheroids for general values of the two odd viscosity coefficients. We show that the resulting Hall angles can differ for oblate and prolate spheroids, implying that sedimentation in a diatomic gas subject to a background magnetic field can separate particles according to shape.
tldr: This paper studies odd-viscous Stokes flow around spheroids in a diatomic gas under a magnetic field, showing shape-based separation via Hall angles.
motivation: Understanding how magnetic fields affect transport in neutral diatomic gases (Senftleben–Beenakker effect) and exploring potential applications for particle separation by shape.
method: Perturbative expansion around spherical solution and Lorentz reciprocal theorem to compute lift forces on oblate and prolate spheroids for general odd viscosity coefficients.
result: Hall angles differ for oblate and prolate spheroids, enabling shape-based separation during sedimentation in a magnetic field.
conclusion: The study demonstrates a novel mechanism for sorting particles by shape using odd viscosities in a diatomic gas with a magnetic field.

title: Gravitational And Other Shifts Of Whispering-gallery And Gravitational State Interference Patterns Of Light Neutral Particles
authors: V V Nesvizhevsky, J A Pioquinto, K Schreiner, S Baeßler, P Crivelli, F Nez, S Reynaud, P Yzombard, S A Vasiliev And E Widmann
abstract: We discuss the interference patterns of gravitational and whispering gallery quantum states that can be observed with neutrons, atoms, antiatoms, muonium (Mu), positronium (Ps), and other light neutral particles. A gravitational shift of interference patterns of neutron gravitational and whispering-gallery states can be easily observed with cold, very cold, or ultracold neutrons. The developed methods can be used for observing/searching for other shifts in fundamental neutron physics experiments, for instance, for measuring the gravitational constant or constraining the neutron electric charge. A series of such measurements will be made with neutrons at the PF1B, PF2, D17 facilities at the ILL. A peculiar feature of analogous atomic (anti-atomic) experiments is the much smaller effective critical energies of the materials of mirrors for (anti)atoms. We evaluated parameters that make a measurement of the hydrogen and antihydrogen whispering-gallery states and their gravitational shifts feasible. A series of such measurements will be made with hydrogen and deuterium atoms by the GRASIAN collaboration in Vienna and Turku. A similar measurement with antihydrogen atoms may be of interest for the GBAR experiment, the ASACUSA experiment, which is producing a beam of slow antihydrogen atoms, and other experiments at CERN that study the gravitational properties of antimatter. Quantum reflection (QR) of Mu and Ps from material surfaces opens the possibility of observing whispering-gallery states, although such measurements remain experimentally challenging. Because of the small masses of Mu and Ps, their effective critical energies of the mirror materials are much higher for them than the effective critical energies for hydrogen and other atoms. The observation of gravitational shifts of such states is particularly demanding because of the extremely short lifetimes of these systems. Measurements of whispering gallery states with all these atoms and particles yield precise and detailed information on the QR properties of materials, providing valuable input for both fundamental physics and surface physics studies.
tldr: This paper discusses gravitational and whispering gallery state interference patterns for light neutral particles, focusing on experimental measurements of gravitational shifts and quantum reflection.
motivation: To explore gravitational and other shifts in interference patterns of quantum states of neutrons, atoms, and antiatoms, which could provide tests of fundamental physics and surface properties.
method: The authors analyze the feasibility of observing gravitational shifts in whispering-gallery and gravitational states using various particles, considering effective critical energies and quantum reflection.
result: They find that gravitational shifts can be observed with neutrons and hydrogen/antihydrogen atoms, while muonium and positronium present experimental challenges due to short lifetimes.
conclusion: Measurements of these states can yield precise information on quantum reflection and fundamental constants, but the work is primarily experimental and phenomenological, not advancing quantum information or thermodynamics theory.

title: Readjustment Of Intrinsic Activity Parameters Governs The Rectified Transport In Asymmetric Ratchets
authors: Yunyan Chen, Xiaoyuan Yu, Fengguo Li And Baoquan Ai
abstract: The rectified transport of active Brownian particles (ABPs) in asymmetric ratchets has been extensively studied. However, most existing literature regulates rectification by designing different structural boundaries. In this work, we shift the research perspective to the internal properties of ABPs and explore the influence of their internal physical parameters on the transport process. Using the vibration-driven vehicle (VDV) as a macroscopic experimental model for ABPs, we systematically adjust the overall mass and position of center of mass of the VDV to reveal its underlying dynamic mechanism. Through long-time dynamic tracking, we identify a ‘parameters readjustment effect’: an increase in mass weakens the particle’s average velocity and persistence length, ultimately driving the active system into a noise-dominated macroscopic localized state. More importantly, the shift of the center of mass induces persistent translational–rotational coupling in the VDV, leading to an anomalous non-monotonic reentrant phase transition in the rectification probability of the system. Our study reveals that this anomalous transport law is fundamentally governed by the dynamic spatial competition between the intrinsic chiral orbit radius of the VDV and the geometric characteristic scale of the channel. Coarse-grained ABP numerical simulations reproduce the overall experimental trends. This work indicates that load-induced parameters evolution is not merely a physical perturbation, but a core dimension that determines macroscopic transport behavior, providing physical insights and principles for going beyond purely geometric design constraints and designing efficient active rectification systems.
tldr: This paper studies rectified transport of active Brownian particles in asymmetric ratchets by adjusting internal parameters like mass and center of mass, revealing a 'parameters readjustment effect' and anomalous reentrant phase transitions.
motivation: Most existing work on active ratchets focuses on structural boundaries; this work shifts to internal properties of active particles to understand their influence on transport.
method: Using a vibration-driven vehicle (VDV) as a macroscopic experimental model for active Brownian particles, the authors systematically vary mass and center of mass position, perform long-time dynamic tracking, and complement with coarse-grained numerical simulations.
result: Increasing mass reduces average velocity and persistence length, leading to a noise-dominated localized state. Shifting the center of mass induces translational-rotational coupling, causing a non-monotonic reentrant phase transition in rectification probability.
conclusion: Load-induced parameter evolution is a core determinant of macroscopic transport behavior, offering principles for designing efficient active rectification systems beyond geometric constraints.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies uniaxial-stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on the coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration in frustrated magnets, and to explore the strong coupling between magnetic order and lattice elasticity.
method: The authors apply uniaxial stress to PdCrO2 and perform x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction to characterize structural and magnetic changes.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice (Young's modulus increases by GPa, Poisson ratio drops).
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked under stress, likely due to nesting of the Fermi surface, suggesting that other frustrated magnets may exhibit similar magnetoelastic coupling.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. Using in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution, we directly image the real potential profile across an entire graphene device, including regions covered by AlOx and TiOx nanometer-thick overlayers. Tracking the valence band edge under current bias and gate voltage enables quantitative analysis of internal field evolution via a spectroscopic screening factor, revealing an up to more than 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene covered with oxides, in agreement with transport measurements. This demonstrates local reconfiguration of electric fields in graphene for advanced two-dimensional (2D) device engineering and circuitry, while our operando circuit spectroscopy measurements provide a generic means to uncover intricate potential landscapes and carrier redistribution in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.
tldr: This paper uses photoemission microscopy to directly visualize the electrostatic potential profile in graphene devices with oxide overlayers, revealing field suppression.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic electrostatic landscape in graphene devices is crucial for optimizing electronic and spintronic performance, but indirect transport measurements lack spatial detail.
method: In operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution was used to image the valence band edge across graphene devices with AlOx and TiOx overlayers under bias and gate voltage.
result: The electric field in graphene covered with oxides is suppressed by up to 50% compared to bare graphene, consistent with transport measurements.
conclusion: Operando circuit spectroscopy provides a generic method to uncover potential landscapes in 2D devices, enabling advanced engineering of graphene circuits.

title: Probing Individual Phonon-polaritonic Nanoparticle-on-mirror Cavities By Infrared Nanospectroscopy
authors: Isabel Pascual Robledo, Iker Herrero Le\'on, Karol Ko{\l}ataj, Guillermo P. Acuna, Javier Aizpurua, Philippe Roelli, Rainer Hillenbrand
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities enable extreme light confinement and strong light-matter interactions, but their realization with phonon-polariton materials in the mid-infrared spectral range remains largely unexplored. Here, we use nano-FTIR spectroscopy to study the near-field response of individual phononic NPoM cavities formed by gold nanoparticles on a quartz substrate supporting phonon-polaritons. By placing a metal tip on top of the NPoM and recording the tip-scattered field, we observe two reproducible cavity resonances, identified as the fundamental and a second-order antenna modes by numerical simulations. The calculations show that, in absence of the tip, the NPoM cavity exhibits ultrasmall mode volumes ([MATH] nm[MATH]) and high quality factors ([MATH]), resulting in extraordinary field intensity enhancements ([MATH]) and Purcell factors ([MATH]). They also indicate that the nano-FTIR tip enables efficient excitation and readout of these phononic NPoM modes without perturbing them, while enhancing the intrinsic local field intensity in the NPoM gap by two orders of magnitude. Our results establish phononic NPoM cavities as a promising platform for mid-infrared nanophotonics and pave the way for ultrasensitive vibrational spectroscopy based on nano-FTIR measurements of individual cavities.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies phonon-polaritonic nanoparticle-on-mirror cavities in the mid-infrared using nano-FTIR spectroscopy, demonstrating extreme field confinement and high Purcell factors.
motivation: Nanoparticle-on-mirror cavities with phonon-polariton materials in the mid-infrared are largely unexplored, yet they promise strong light-matter interactions for nanophotonics and vibrational spectroscopy.
method: The authors use nano-FTIR spectroscopy with a metal tip to excite and read out cavity modes of gold nanoparticles on a quartz substrate, supported by numerical simulations.
result: Two cavity resonances are observed, identified as fundamental and second-order antenna modes. Simulations show ultrasmall mode volumes, high quality factors, and extraordinary field enhancements and Purcell factors.
conclusion: Phononic NPoM cavities are established as a promising platform for mid-infrared nanophotonics and ultrasensitive vibrational spectroscopy.

title: From Bayes' Rule To Bayes Rules: Optimal Information Processing And Axiomatic Foundations Beyond Probability
authors: Badr-Eddine Ch\'erief-Abdellatif Jeremie Houssineau
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops principled updating rules for possibilistic inference, where uncertainty about a fixed parameter is represented by a possibility function, the maxitive analogue of a probability distribution, and comparisons are made pointwise via a partial order. From two complementary foundations, an information-conservation viewpoint and an axiomatic viewpoint, we derive the same canonical update: the posterior is the prior-likelihood product followed by supremum normalisation. The two derivations agree for an arbitrary loss, differing only in where the learning-rate parameter enters. This parameter controls epistemic strength and is not identifiable from the normalising evidence alone, clarifying the role of analogous learning-rate parameters in generalised Bayesian updating.
tldr: This paper develops possibilistic inference updating rules based on information-conservation and axiomatic foundations, extending Bayesian reasoning to possibility functions.
motivation: To provide principled updating rules for possibilistic inference, where uncertainty is represented by possibility functions rather than probability distributions, and to clarify the role of learning-rate parameters in generalized Bayesian updating.
method: The authors derive a canonical update rule from two complementary foundations: an information-conservation viewpoint and an axiomatic viewpoint, both yielding the same posterior as the prior-likelihood product followed by supremum normalization.
result: The two derivations agree for an arbitrary loss, differing only in where the learning-rate parameter enters, which controls epistemic strength and is not identifiable from normalizing evidence alone.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for possibilistic inference and clarifies the role of learning-rate parameters in generalized Bayesian updating.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Empowered Wireless Sensor Networking For 6g Closed-Loop Controls
authors: Chengleyang Lei, Wei Feng, Yunfei Chen, Yongxu Zhu, Ning Ge, Shi Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robots are increasingly deployed in remote or hazardous areas for mission-critical control tasks. Due to their limited individual capabilities, they have to rely on other field sensors to obtain the state information of targets, and also a dedicated edge information hub (EIH) to enable information exchange, sensing data analysis and control command generation. Such configuration follows a sensing-communication-computing-control (SC3) closed loop. To optimize the whole closed-loop performance, this paper minimizes the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control cost by designing the sensor-to-EIH bandwidth allocation. Specifically, we first model the distortion noise caused by limited communication data rate based on the mutual information theory. Next, under the control policy based on the Kalman filter and LQR controller, we formulate the control process as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based sensor-to-EIH bandwidth allocation scheme. The proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm is utilized to train the DRL agent. Simulation results are provided to show the superiority of the proposed DRL-based scheme.
tldr: This paper uses deep reinforcement learning to optimize bandwidth allocation in wireless sensor networks for 6G closed-loop control, minimizing LQR control cost.
motivation: Robots in remote/hazardous areas need efficient sensing-communication-computing-control loops; optimizing bandwidth allocation can improve control performance.
method: Models distortion noise via mutual information, formulates control as POMDP, and uses PPO algorithm to allocate sensor-to-EIH bandwidth.
result: Simulations show the DRL-based scheme outperforms baselines in reducing LQR control cost.
conclusion: DRL-based bandwidth allocation effectively enhances closed-loop control performance in wireless sensor networks.

title: Optimization And Deep Learning Based Resource Allocation For UAV-Aided Wireless Communication With Rotatable Antenna Array
authors: Fengcheng Pei, Lin Xiang, Anja Klein, Robert Schober
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-antenna unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-aided communication presents a promising solution to increase the system capacity and improve the quality of service (QoS) of the future wireless networks. In this paper, we equip a UAV platform with a rotatable antenna array (RAA), which can be rotated flexibly in three-dimensional (3D) space via an onboard gimbal, enabling additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) for improving multiuser signal transmission and interference management. Compared with a conventional fixed antenna array (FAA), the RAA can proactively align users with the high-gain region of its antenna elements and reduce the spatial channel correlations among users. To demonstrate the advantages of RAA, we jointly design the RAA orientation and beamforming to maximize the sum-rate of multiple users subject to per-user QoS constraints. The formulated problem is highly nonconvex and exhibits strong coupling between the RAA orientation and beamforming variables. To solve this challenging problem, we propose first an optimization framework based on the penalty dual decomposition (PDD) method to iteratively optimize RAA orientation and beamforming. While the optimization framework yields high reliability in QoS satisfaction and favorable sum-rate performance, its iterative nature may hinder real-time deployment. To accelerate the joint design and preserve a high-quality solution, we further propose a deep learning (DL) framework based on graph neural networks (GNNs). Simulation results demonstrate that RAAs significantly outperform FAAs in UAV-aided communication. Additionally, the proposed optimization framework is capable of satisfying stringent QoS requirements with high reliability, while the proposed DL framework attains comparable sum-rate performance with substantially reduced computation time and exhibits robustness to user position information errors.
tldr: This paper proposes optimization and deep learning methods for resource allocation in UAV-aided wireless communication with rotatable antenna arrays.
motivation: To improve system capacity and quality of service in future wireless networks by leveraging the additional spatial degrees of freedom from rotatable antenna arrays on UAVs.
method: Jointly designs RAA orientation and beamforming using a penalty dual decomposition optimization framework and a graph neural network-based deep learning framework.
result: RAAs significantly outperform fixed antenna arrays; the optimization framework satisfies stringent QoS requirements reliably, while the DL framework achieves comparable sum-rate with reduced computation time and robustness to errors.
conclusion: Rotatable antenna arrays combined with efficient optimization or deep learning can enhance UAV-aided wireless communication performance.

title: Neural And Spectral Operator Surrogates On Gaussian Spaces
authors: Carlo Marcati, Mario Mari\'c, Christoph Schwab, Jakob Zech
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove expression rate bounds of finite-parametric, spectral and neural surrogates for holomorphic maps between separable Hilbert spaces. The surrogates have an encoder-approximator-decoder architecture, with Karhunen-Lo\'{e}ve encoders and frame decoders. We prove expression rate bounds for two classes of finite-parametric surrogates: i) spectral surrogates obtained by N-term truncations of Wiener polynomial chaos expansions and ii) neural surrogates obtained by approximation of parametric maps with deep feedforward neural networks, ReLU and RePU activation functions and uniformly bounded weights. We work under an algebraic decay assumption on the eigenvalues of the covariance of the Gaussian measure on the input space. We obtain convergence rates for mean-square errors, and additionally in first-order Gaussian Sobolev spaces, to account for errors in the approximation of gradients.
tldr: This paper studies approximation rates of spectral and neural surrogates for holomorphic maps on Gaussian spaces, focusing on operator learning in infinite-dimensional settings.
motivation: To develop efficient surrogate models for parametric maps arising in uncertainty quantification and PDEs with random inputs.
method: Proves expression rate bounds for spectral surrogates (Wiener polynomial chaos) and neural surrogates (deep feedforward networks with ReLU/RePU) using Karhunen-Loève encoders and frame decoders under eigenvalue decay assumptions.
result: Obtains convergence rates for mean-square errors and first-order Gaussian Sobolev norms, showing algebraic rates depending on eigenvalue decay.
conclusion: Both spectral and neural surrogates achieve comparable approximation rates, with neural networks offering flexibility for high-dimensional problems.

title: Mlqenabler: Enabling Secure Machine Learning Queries Over Encrypted Database In Cloud Computing
authors: Xu Zhou, Haoyang Chen, Xinyu Lei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cloud computing, the public cloud service providers (CSPs) can provide cloud storage as the primary service while providing additional machine learning (ML)-based services by using the clients' data in storage. This business model extends the border of cloud computing services and brings in new business growth possibilities. Although it is promising, the model also brings in security concerns since the public commercial cloud cannot be fully trusted. For example, the public commercial clouds may sell clients' sensitive data to the government or other companies. To address the security concerns, an immediate solution is to require clients to encrypt their datasets before outsourcing to the cloud. However, if a database is formally encrypted, then the database contains only pseudorandom numbers, making it impossible to enable ML over it. In this project, we propose MLQENABLER (ML Queries Enabler) scheme to enable secure ML queries over encrypted database in cloud storage. MLQENABLER employs an index-aid approach to achieve security and ML capability simultaneously. Our initial experiments show that MLQENABLER achieves an acceptable security level while incurring only a slight ML performance degradation.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to enable secure machine learning queries over encrypted databases in cloud computing.
motivation: Cloud service providers cannot be fully trusted, so clients encrypt their data, but encrypted data prevents machine learning. The paper aims to enable ML on encrypted data.
method: The scheme uses an index-aid approach to allow ML queries on encrypted databases while maintaining security.
result: Initial experiments show acceptable security with slight ML performance degradation.
conclusion: The proposed scheme balances security and ML capability, but further work is needed.

title: Threshold Authorization Without Threshold Signatures: Signature-Agnostic Mpc Custody
authors: Dariia Porechna
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital-asset custody has been built on threshold multi-party approval: no operation proceeds unless [MATH] of [MATH] parties approve, and fewer than t compromised parties can neither authorize nor learn the authorization secret. Threshold signature schemes (TSS) have been the standard mechanism, but the post-quantum transition disrupts this model: standardized hash-based signatures resist efficient threshold signing, and lattice-based threshold protocols remain an emerging research track. We present a dual-gate architecture that separates member authentication from threshold authorization. Each member signs its approval with an ordinary signature under any EUF-CMA scheme; the quorum jointly produces a threshold seal from Shamir-shared secrets bound to the operation. The seal is the base instance of a programmable authorization computation: simple quorum is the minimal policy, while richer policies can evaluate secret-shared state without making the member-signature scheme part of that computation. The signature scheme is a deployment parameter: migrating from ECDSA to SLH-DSA or ML-DSA is a key rotation, not a protocol redesign, and members holding keys in commodity HSMs participate through the standard sign API. The architecture can be deployed wherever the asset-control path supports programmable verification, such as smart contracts, vault modules, or HSMs guarding a master key, and produces an enforcement-layer authorization rather than a native chain signature. Below-threshold secrecy is information-theoretic; an adversary holding [MATH] signing keys but no coefficient shares still cannot produce the seal.
tldr: A dual-gate architecture for threshold authorization in digital-asset custody that separates member authentication from threshold signing, enabling post-quantum signature agility.
motivation: Threshold signature schemes (TSS) face challenges with post-quantum signatures like hash-based and lattice-based schemes, which either resist efficient threshold signing or are not yet mature. The paper aims to provide a signature-agnostic authorization mechanism that can easily migrate between signature schemes.
method: The architecture uses ordinary signatures for member authentication and a threshold seal from Shamir-shared secrets for authorization, decoupling the signature scheme from the threshold logic. The seal is a programmable authorization computation that can implement various policies.
result: The architecture allows signature scheme migration via key rotation without protocol redesign, supports commodity HSMs, and provides information-theoretic secrecy below threshold.
conclusion: The proposed architecture offers a practical solution for post-quantum transition in digital-asset custody, but its focus is on applied cryptography and system design rather than quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Trace: A Two-Channel Robust Attribution Watermark Via Complementary Embeddings For LLM-Agent Trajectories
authors: Zheng Gao, Xiaoyu Li, Xiaoyan Feng, Jiaojiao Jiang, Yang Song, Yulei Sui, Zhenchang Xing, Liming Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents reach users through resellers, who may rebrand a developer's agent or substitute a cheaper model. When provenance is disputed, attribution rests on the trajectory log (the record of tool calls, observations, and executed actions, not the model's reasoning), which the reseller stores and processes to meter usage. A watermark must therefore survive an adversary with full read/write access to the very evidence it is detected from; existing agent watermarks do not, as their attribution is read straight off that log. We present TRACE, to our knowledge the first agent watermark that is distortion-free in its action choices, self-synchronizing under deletion, and unconditionally invariant under rewriting. Deletion desynchronizes a position-derived key and rewriting alters content, so a deletion-robust key must come from content and a rewrite-robust key from position, and no single key serves both. A trajectory, however, has room for two watermarks. TRACE superposes a selection channel that sets which action is chosen, keyed on local content with a distortion-free sampler, so the agent's distribution is provably unchanged and detection resynchronizes after deletions, and a tally channel that sets how many records each decision group holds, keyed on the log's skeleton alone, which no rewriting can touch. We prove this behavioral watermark's signal is bought with decision entropy, each decision paying at least half its entropy and deterministic decisions nothing, and that erasing both channels forces the reseller to corrupt the trajectories it resells. On ToolBench and ALFWorld, TRACE matches the unwatermarked agent's success rate while its selection channel reaches detection scores near z = 100 on long-horizon trajectories, stays detectable under 70% step deletion, and keeps a tally channel exactly unchanged under LLM rewriting of any strength.
tldr: This paper proposes a watermarking scheme for LLM agent trajectories that is robust to deletion and rewriting attacks.
motivation: Existing watermarks for LLM agents fail because resellers can modify the trajectory log, which is the only evidence for attribution. A robust watermark must survive full read/write access to the log.
method: TRACE uses two complementary channels: a selection channel that embeds a watermark via distortion-free action selection keyed on local content, and a tally channel that embeds a watermark via the number of records per decision group keyed on the log skeleton.
result: TRACE matches the unwatermarked agent's success rate, achieves detection scores near z=100 on long trajectories, remains detectable under 70% step deletion, and is invariant under LLM rewriting.
conclusion: TRACE is the first agent watermark that is distortion-free, self-synchronizing under deletion, and unconditionally invariant under rewriting, providing robust attribution for LLM agents.

title: Multi-Sender Bayesian Persuasion With Imperfect Information
authors: Andra Siva Sai Teja, Ganesh Ghalme, Sujit Gujar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a multi-sender Bayesian persuasion problem with one receiver and several strategic senders. The underlying ground state has multiple components, each privately observed by a different sender, while the receiver holds a common prior over the joint state space. Senders simultaneously choose signaling policies, and the receiver takes an action based on the posterior induced by the signals; each is sampled independently from the sender's signaling policy. We analyze the game induced by the receiver's straightforward policy, which selects a receiver-optimal action at every posterior. In particular, we characterize the senders' best responses under the straightforward policy and identify conditions on the prior that induce a fully informative equilibrium; i.e., truthfully reporting the ground truth is an equilibrium strategy for every sender. These conditions capture cases in which senders' incentives are sufficiently aligned to enable full revelation without additional commitment from the receiver. The important contribution of this paper is to analyze games induced by a more general (possibly randomized) class of action policies that the receiver commits to before senders choose their signaling strategies. We show that this commitment power fundamentally changes the problem. In particular, we show that for any prior over the joint state space, the receiver can construct action policies that maximize her payoff while ensuring a fully informative equilibrium.
tldr: This paper studies multi-sender Bayesian persuasion with imperfect information, focusing on equilibrium analysis and receiver commitment.
motivation: To understand how multiple strategic senders with private information can influence a receiver's decision through signaling, and how the receiver can design action policies to ensure full information revelation.
method: The authors model the problem as a game where senders choose signaling policies and the receiver commits to an action policy; they characterize conditions for fully informative equilibrium and construct optimal receiver policies.
result: They identify conditions on the prior that induce fully informative equilibrium under straightforward receiver policy, and show that with commitment, the receiver can always achieve a fully informative equilibrium.
conclusion: Receiver commitment power can fundamentally change the game, enabling full information revelation even when senders' incentives are not aligned.

title: Visualization Of The Zhang–Rice Singlet, Electronic Molecules And Cooper Pair Formation In A Cuprate Superconductor
authors: Shusen Ye
Jianfa Zhao
Zhiheng Yao
Sixuan Chen
Runze Yu
Zehao Dong
Zhenqi Hao
Xintong Li
Luchuan Shi
Qingqing Liu
Changqing Jin
Yayu Wang
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: This paper visualizes the Zhang-Rice singlet, electronic molecules, and Cooper pair formation in a cuprate superconductor using scanning tunneling microscopy.
motivation: Understanding how doped holes evolve into Cooper pairs in cuprate superconductors is a long-standing problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to directly image the electronic structure of a cuprate compound at different doping levels.
result: They observe the formation of Zhang-Rice singlets, electronic molecules, and the emergence of Cooper pairs as doping increases.
conclusion: The study provides direct experimental evidence for the microscopic process of Cooper pair formation in cuprates, advancing the understanding of high-temperature superconductivity.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
authors: A. Jadbabaie
S. Ebadi
R. F. Garcia Ruiz
N. R. Hutzler
A. M. Jayich
J. T. Singh
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This Perspective discusses the use of radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore new avenues for fundamental physics at energy scales complementary to high-energy colliders, leveraging advances in molecular quantum control.
method: The paper reviews experimental techniques for producing, trapping, and controlling radioactive molecules, and discusses how these enable precision measurements of symmetry-violating effects.
result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei offer enhanced sensitivity to certain fundamental symmetry violations, providing a promising platform for new physics searches.
conclusion: Advances in molecular quantum control make radioactive molecules a viable laboratory for fundamental physics, complementing collider-based searches.

title: When Vacuum Breaks: A Self-Consistency Test For Astrophysical Environments In Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals
authors: Lorenzo Copparoni, Rohit S. Chandramouli, And Enrico Barausse
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Copparoni, Rohit S. Chandramouli, and Enrico Barausse

Gravitational-wave signals are typically interpreted under the vacuum hypothesis, i.e., assuming negligible influence from the astrophysical environment. This assumption is expected to break down for low-frequency sources such as extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs), which are prime targets for the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests the vacuum hypothesis for gravitational wave signals from extreme mass ratio inspirals, finding that astrophysical environments can significantly affect the waveform.
motivation: Gravitational wave signals are typically interpreted assuming negligible environmental influence, but for low-frequency sources like EMRIs this assumption may break down.
method: The authors develop a self-consistency test to assess whether the vacuum hypothesis holds for given EMRI parameters, considering environmental effects such as accretion disks or dark matter.
result: They find that for certain astrophysical environments, the vacuum hypothesis fails, meaning environmental effects must be accounted for in waveform modeling.
conclusion: Environmental effects are important for accurate EMRI waveform interpretation, and the proposed test can help identify when the vacuum approximation is insufficient.

title: Multiferroicity In The Two-Dimensional Limit In Hexagonal ${\mathrm{LuFeO}}_{3}$ Films
authors: Huilin Lai, Junyu Tan, Jinfeng Zhai, Yang Shi, Lili Feng, Huanyu Zhang, Chuanrui Huo, Chuhang Liu, Lijun Wu, Lifeng Yin, Hangwen Guo, Jun Chen, Xiaoshan Xu, Jun Zhao, Yimei Zhu, Shiqing Deng, Wenbin Wang, And Jian Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Huilin Lai, Junyu Tan, Jinfeng Zhai, Yang Shi, Lili Feng, Huanyu Zhang, Chuanrui Huo, Chuhang Liu, Lijun Wu, Lifeng Yin, Hangwen Guo, Jun Chen, Xiaoshan Xu, Jun Zhao, Yimei Zhu, Shiqing Deng, Wenbin Wang, and Jian Shen

Multiferroic oxides, which host coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders, are central to understanding correlated quantum phenomena. Yet, as thickness approaches the two-dimensional (2D) limit, both ferroelectricity and magnetism are generally expected to be strongly suppressed by depolarization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of multiferroicity in two-dimensional LuFeO3 films, demonstrating coexisting ferroelectric and magnetic orders at the monolayer limit.
motivation: Multiferroic oxides are important for understanding correlated quantum phenomena, but ferroelectricity and magnetism are expected to be suppressed in the 2D limit; this work aims to test whether they can persist.
method: The authors fabricate hexagonal LuFeO3 films down to monolayer thickness and characterize their structural, ferroelectric, and magnetic properties using various experimental techniques.
result: They find that both ferroelectric and magnetic orders coexist in the 2D limit, contrary to theoretical expectations of suppression.
conclusion: The discovery opens up possibilities for studying multiferroicity in atomically thin materials and may have implications for nanoelectronic devices.

title: Three-Dimensional Wide-Bandwidth Quantum Energy Truncation Terahertz Coherence Tomography
authors: Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, And Andreas Mandelis
abstract:
Author(s): Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, and Andreas Mandelis

We report a quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography technique that enables highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses. The method exploits resonant photon loss when the emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta. Reflected THz radiation is rec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026901] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A terahertz imaging technique using quantum energy truncation for molecular-specific tomography.
motivation: To achieve highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses for imaging applications.
method: Exploits resonant photon loss when emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta, and uses reflected THz radiation for coherence tomography.
result: Demonstrates three-dimensional wide-bandwidth quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography.
conclusion: The technique enables molecular-specific THz imaging with high localization.

title: Barium Autoionization For Efficient Ion Trap Loading
authors: Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, And Wesley C. Campbell
abstract:
Author(s): Zachary J. Wall, Justin D. Piel, Samuel R. Vizvary, Michael Bareian, Steven Diaz, Elijah Mossman, Anthony Ransford, Chris H. Greene, Eric R. Hudson, and Wesley C. Campbell

We report a theoretical and experimental investigation of autoionizing resonances from the [MATH] manifold in neutral barium for efficient loading of ion traps. Our calculations predict large resonant cross sections for many narrow autoionizing reson…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013102] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates autoionizing resonances in barium for efficient ion trap loading, focusing on atomic physics and experimental techniques.
motivation: Efficient loading of ion traps is crucial for quantum computing and sensing, but current methods are inefficient; this work aims to improve loading rates using autoionization.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations of autoionizing resonance cross sections with experimental measurements in a barium atomic beam, demonstrating enhanced ionization efficiency.
result: They identify and characterize narrow autoionizing resonances that yield large resonant cross sections, leading to more efficient ion production for trap loading.
conclusion: The proposed autoionization scheme offers a practical method to significantly improve ion trap loading efficiency, benefiting quantum information platforms.

title: Multistage Development Of Short-range Spin Correlations And Weak Magnetic Order In The Two Coupled Trillium Lattices Of ${\mathrm{K}}_{2}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}({\mathrm{MoO}}_{4}){({\mathrm{PO}}_{4})}_{2}$
authors: J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

Trillium lattices, where magnetic ions form a chiral network of corner-sharing triangles, offer a three-dimensional magnetic framework that can host fragile classical spin-liquid states. Herein, we report on the magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and muon spin relaxation $(…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034410] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of a frustrated trillium lattice material, focusing on short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order.
motivation: Trillium lattices are candidate hosts for classical spin-liquid states, and understanding their magnetic behavior is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and muon spin relaxation measurements to characterize the spin correlations and magnetic order.
result: They observe multistage development of short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order, but no clear spin-liquid behavior.
conclusion: The material exhibits complex magnetic ordering without evidence of a spin-liquid state, contributing to the understanding of frustrated magnetism.

title: Nonlinear Anisotropy In Phase-tuned Wide-gap Halides
authors: L. Landivar Scott, L. M. Vogl, C. Klenke, S. Puri, And H. Nakamura
abstract:
Author(s): L. Landivar Scott, L. M. Vogl, C. Klenke, S. Puri, and H. Nakamura

Silver iodide (AgI) thin films offer a compelling platform for studying nonlinear optical phenomena due to their intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice and direct band gap. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties of AgI thin films grown by physical vapor deposition that selectively produ…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045408] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear optical properties of silver iodide thin films, focusing on nonlinear anisotropy in phase-tuned wide-gap halides.
motivation: Silver iodide thin films offer a platform for studying nonlinear optical phenomena due to their noncentrosymmetric lattice and direct band gap.
method: The authors grow AgI thin films by physical vapor deposition and characterize their nonlinear optical properties.
result: The paper reports on the nonlinear anisotropy observed in these films.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding nonlinear optics in halide materials but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fine Structure Of The Cyclotron Resonance In Heterobilayers Of Proximitized Graphene And Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: M. A. Rakitskii, K. S. Denisov, And N. S. Averkiev
abstract:
Author(s): M. A. Rakitskii, K. S. Denisov, and N. S. Averkiev

A monolayer graphene and its Dirac electrons can be equipped with an enhanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) when proximitized by other van der Waals (vdW) materials, such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). In this work we analyze the features of the cyclotron resonance (CR) absorption at quanti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051403] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the fine structure of cyclotron resonance in graphene/TMD heterobilayers with enhanced spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: To understand how proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling affects the cyclotron resonance absorption in graphene-based heterostructures.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Landau level structure and optical absorption spectra of graphene proximitized by TMDs, considering the interplay of SOC and magnetic field.
result: They predict a fine structure in the cyclotron resonance peaks due to spin-orbit coupling, with characteristic splitting and selection rules.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the electronic properties of proximitized graphene, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Origin Of Muon Spin Relaxation And Frequency Shift In Frozen Water Explained By Spin-dipole Quantum Coherences
authors: Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, And Koichiro Shimomura
abstract:
Author(s): Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, and Koichiro Shimomura

To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water with temperature, we performed weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation ([MATH]) measurements over a temperature range of 220 K to 300 K. Using a conventional model with a phenomenological relaxation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034106] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water using spin-dipole quantum coherences, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water across temperatures, which is a problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation measurements were performed over 220 K to 300 K, and a model incorporating spin-dipole quantum coherences was used.
result: The model successfully explains the observed relaxation and frequency shift, attributing them to quantum coherences between muon and proton spins.
conclusion: The study provides a microscopic understanding of muon behavior in water, but does not contribute to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Model-free Analysis Of Complex Systems Using Delayed-feedback Echo State Network
authors: Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, And Xu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, and Xu Xu

Investigating the dynamical behavior of complex systems from data poses formidable challenges in the field of nonlinear science. This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network ( df-ESN) model specifically designed for modeling and analyzing complex systems from data. The df-ESN introdu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014204] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network for modeling complex systems from data, focusing on nonlinear dynamics and machine learning.
motivation: Investigating dynamical behavior of complex systems from data is challenging; existing methods may not capture long-term dependencies effectively.
method: The authors introduce a delayed-feedback echo state network (df-ESN) that incorporates time-delayed feedback into the reservoir to improve modeling of complex systems.
result: The df-ESN demonstrates improved performance in predicting and analyzing complex dynamical systems compared to standard ESNs.
conclusion: The delayed-feedback mechanism enhances the capability of echo state networks for model-free analysis of complex systems.

title: Distinct Phenomenon On Chaos Synchrony: Chirality
authors: Gualberto C. Solís-Perales And Ricardo Femat
abstract:
Author(s): Gualberto C. Solís-Perales and Ricardo Femat

Among others, chirality is a property of organometallic molecules whose main feature is that the spatial superposition is exclusively observed through a specular plane. A specular plane is a physical kind of subspace onto which chiral objects can already be superposed. That is, chirality corresponds…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies chirality in the context of chaos synchrony, a topic unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
