abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and demonstrates its application to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications, breaking the traditional bandwidth limit of resonant modes.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]
authors: Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, and Frédéric Merkt
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 029901] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on ion-molecule reaction rates at low temperatures, with no relevance to quantum information theory.
motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K, which is a topic in physical chemistry.
method: The erratum likely corrects errors or clarifies data from the original experimental or theoretical study.
result: The erratum provides corrections to the published results.
conclusion: The paper is a correction notice and does not contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces, analogous to the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To understand and design the deformation of mechanical metamaterials on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new framework for designing materials with desired deformation properties.
conclusion: The approach offers a different path for materials design, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and relate it to bulk hydrogel behavior.
result: They develop a force-response model that explains fatigue behavior and provides design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work offers insights into molecular-level fatigue mechanisms and practical guidelines for creating tougher soft materials.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of wood-derived nanocrystal films through a vapor training process that induces mesopore changes.
motivation: Understanding and improving the plasticity of nanocrystal films is important for shaping wood-derived materials into desired forms.
method: A vapor training process is applied to wood-derived films, and the resulting changes in mesopore structure and mechanical properties are characterized.
result: The vapor training process leads to improved plasticity and better shaping of the films due to mesopore changes.
conclusion: The hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films can be enhanced by controlling mesopore structure via vapor training, enabling better formability.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally tracks ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using ultrafast electron diffraction.
motivation: To directly observe and characterize ion diffusion in superionic conductors at ultrafast timescales, linking microscopic dynamics to macroscopic properties.
method: Ultrafast electron diffraction with femtosecond laser pump-probe techniques to monitor structural changes and ion motion in AgCrSe2.
result: Direct spatiotemporal mapping of ion diffusion, revealing the timescales and pathways of ionic motion.
conclusion: The study provides insights into ion transport mechanisms in superionic conductors, aiding design of high-performance materials.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects drive cell extrusion in curved tissues is important for developmental biology and disease.
method: The authors develop a 3D bubbly vertex model to simulate epithelial sheets with curvature and analyze cell shape changes and extrusion events.
result: They find that curvature enhances cell bulging and extrusion at topological defects, with specific patterns depending on defect type.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the mechanobiology of epithelial tissues, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-energy Emission From The Galactic Center
authors: Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, And Régis Terrier
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy emission from the Galactic Center, covering the supermassive black hole, compact sources, and plasma structures.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of the Galactic Center, which is the closest galactic nucleus and a unique laboratory for high-energy astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths (X-ray, gamma-ray, etc.) and theoretical models of emission processes.
result: Summarizes the quiescent and flaring emission from Sgr A*, the properties of plasma bubbles and chimneys, and the interaction with the surrounding molecular zone.
conclusion: The Galactic Center is a rich environment for studying high-energy phenomena, with implications for black hole accretion and cosmic-ray acceleration.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and computational studies to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation and evolution.
result: A unified model emerges where tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heating, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdown.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more robust accelerator structures and other high-voltage vacuum systems.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into QCD, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental results from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: BESIII has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, with recent advances highlighted.
conclusion: The review summarizes current progress and emphasizes the importance of ongoing experiments for validating QCD and discovering new hadrons.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its contributions to planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on multiple scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial that reviews the observatory's achievements through three colloquia.
result: The editorial highlights Arecibo's revolutionary contributions to planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has had a profound and lasting impact on science, and its legacy is celebrated.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the planetary radar system at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on observations of solar system bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes the basics of planetary radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind for over two decades, enabling detailed characterization of many solar system objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss marks the end of an era for ground-based planetary radar.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on various fields of astronomy.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific achievements from the telescope's operation.
result: Highlights major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades enabled sustained scientific breakthroughs over five decades, cementing its legacy.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances achieved using the Arecibo Observatory's radar, lidar, and optical instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere have enabled significant advances in geospace science, and this review aims to consolidate key findings.
method: The paper reviews the incoherent scatter radar technique and summarizes results from Arecibo's suite of instruments, including lidars and optical sensors, applied to ionospheric and magnetospheric studies.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, atomic metal layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are highlighted, demonstrating the observatory's impact.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in advancing geospace science, and its legacy continues through the reviewed contributions.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm rain formation is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors synthesize insights from experiments, theory, and computational models of convection-cloud chambers.
result: Convection-cloud chambers reproduce key turbulent fluctuations and supersaturation conditions relevant to the precipitation bottleneck.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising platform to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales for cloud physics research.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on detection and parameter estimation.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and gravitational waves provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods using ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest predictions for gravitational wave signals and outlines strategies for detection and parameter estimation in a multimessenger context.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from core collapse supernovae is a promising avenue for multimessenger astronomy, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on large-scale structure surveys.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the matter distribution with the CMB dipole, which could indicate a breakdown of the standard model of cosmology.
method: The authors analyze recent catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, comparing the observed dipole in their distribution with the CMB dipole, and review potential biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the ΛCDM model, but further investigation is needed to rule out systematic errors or alternative explanations.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark matter halo dynamics and large-scale structure.
motivation: Dark matter self-interactions are a key aspect of dark sector models, and astrophysical observations provide crucial tests.
method: The review synthesizes results from galaxy-scale to large-scale structure observations, comparing predictions of self-interacting dark matter models with data.
result: Current astrophysical constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections are summarized, showing consistency with some models and tensions with others.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable scenario, but further observational and theoretical work is needed to distinguish it from other models.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and diagnostics.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances over the last decade in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No novel research results; a retrospective on scientific contributions.
conclusion: Physics is a point of view that shapes how we understand the world.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper is a review summarizing key advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, including experimental and theoretical studies.
result: It highlights the effects of added mass, deformable surfaces, turbulence, and surfactants on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but has no relevance to quantum information theory.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify and highlight the role of self-alignment in active systems, which is underexplored compared to neighbor-based alignment.
method: Review of existing models and experiments, presenting a unified mathematical framework for self-alignment.
result: Self-alignment enables novel phenomena like orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with potential applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding morphological instabilities in soft materials is important for materials science and biology, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

title: Phase-controlled Direct Laser Acceleration Enabled By Longitudinal Variation Of The Laser-driven Quasi-static Plasma Magnetic Field
authors: R Bhakta, I-L Yeh, K Tangtartharakul, L Willingale And A Arefiev
abstract: Direct laser acceleration (DLA) enables energy transfer from an ultra-high-intensity laser to plasma electrons and underpins many laser-driven particle and radiation-source concepts. A laser-driven azimuthal plasma magnetic field is a key player in this process: it confines energetic electrons, induces betatron oscillations, and makes possible a resonant interaction between the betatron motion and the laser field. While this betatron resonance can enhance electron energy gain, the gain itself generally drives frequency detuning and promotes largely reversible energy exchange that limits net acceleration. Here we show, using a test-electron model with prescribed fields, that a slow longitudinal increase of the quasi-static plasma magnetic field qualitatively changes DLA by introducing hysteresis in the ratio of the betatron frequency to the laser frequency experienced by the electron, so that this ratio depends on the prior evolution of the electron even at the same energy. This hysteresis enables phase control of the electron-laser energy exchange and suppresses the usual reversibility of DLA, allowing electrons to retain the acquired energy and sustain energy gain without intermittent losses.
tldr: This paper studies phase-controlled direct laser acceleration using longitudinal variation of a laser-driven quasi-static plasma magnetic field.
motivation: Direct laser acceleration (DLA) is important for laser-driven particle and radiation sources, but energy gain is limited by reversible energy exchange. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: Using a test-electron model with prescribed fields, the authors investigate the effect of a slow longitudinal increase of the quasi-static plasma magnetic field on electron dynamics.
result: The longitudinal increase introduces hysteresis in the betatron-to-laser frequency ratio, enabling phase control and suppressing reversibility, allowing sustained energy gain.
conclusion: This approach can enhance net acceleration in DLA by controlling the electron-laser energy exchange.

title: Propagation And Collisionless Damping Of Topologically-protected Surface Plasma Waves In Non-uniformly Magnetized Plasma Columns
authors: Roopendra Singh Rajawat And Gennady Shvets
abstract: Recent theoretical studies revealed the existence of topologically-protected surface plasma waves (TSPWs) in uniformly magnetized cold plasma columns. Reflections-free propagation of the TSPWs along arbitrarily-shaped plasma boundaries oriented perpendicularly to the magnetic field was shown to be preserved even when their collisionless damping by localized upper-hybrid resonances was accounted for. Here we extend this theory to the realistic case of three-dimensional magnetic field produced by finite-sized magnetic coils. We demonstrate that when TSPWs are launched in the direction of the decreasing magnetic field, they are collisionlessly absorbed within a highly localized (evanescent) region as they propagate away from the magnetic coil. We show that the resulting wave reflection can be negligible—in clear contrast with wave reflection from the corresponding evanescence regions of unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
tldr: This paper studies topologically-protected surface plasma waves in non-uniformly magnetized plasma columns, focusing on wave propagation and collisionless damping.
motivation: To extend the theory of topologically-protected surface plasma waves from uniformly magnetized to realistic three-dimensional magnetic fields, and to understand wave absorption and reflection in non-uniform plasmas.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in a cold plasma column with a non-uniform magnetic field produced by finite-sized coils, using a model that accounts for collisionless damping by upper-hybrid resonances.
result: They find that waves launched in the direction of decreasing magnetic field are collisionlessly absorbed in a localized evanescent region, with negligible reflection, contrasting with unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
conclusion: The study demonstrates robust, reflection-free absorption of topologically-protected surface plasma waves in realistic non-uniform magnetic fields, which may have implications for plasma heating and wave control.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical gas sensing technique using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component detection.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.
method: The authors use two continuous-wave lasers modulated at the same frequency with a 45° phase difference, co-exciting a quartz tuning fork. The piezoelectric signal is orthogonally demodulated to decouple the two gas concentration signals.
result: The sensor achieves linear responses for methane and acetylene with low systematic errors (0.54% and 0.79%) and detection limits of 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, respectively.
conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection with a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling.

tldr: This paper models the emergence and suppression of human cannibalism using a formal trade-off framework.
motivation: Cannibalism recurs in human history but is rarely persistent; the authors aim to explain this pattern.
method: The authors develop a formal model analyzing the costs and benefits of cannibalism, incorporating cultural taboos.
result: The model shows that cannibalism can emerge under certain ecological conditions but is suppressed by strong taboos due to long-term social costs.

tldr: This paper studies sleep-dependent motor memory consolidation and its disruption by epileptic spikes in human epilepsy, with no connection to quantum information theory.
